arguments.index: edx, 32-bit index; the zero test is on edx, and the value is forwarded to the selector as esi
arguments.obj: rdi, outer object pointer; only its +0x40 field is read, and only on the nonzero-index path
arguments.source: rsi, record-source pointer; its +0x20, +0x28, +0x40 and +0x48 fields are read, and only on the nonzero-index path

callees_not_modelled.selector_0x5f6c2a0: called once on the nonzero-index path with (selector object, esi = index, rdx = record 1 pointer, rcx = record 2 pointer); its return is inverted by this wrapper. The selector's own semantics are pinned by the RE-001 later-group predicate item and are NOT re-claimed here; the model takes selector results as an oracle input. The selector tail-jumps to the 964-byte dispatch 0x5f6a820, whose own semantics are NOT pinned by this item.

selector.note: this wrapper's site is 0x5ebd196; the later-group predicate 0x5f6d600's site is 0x5f6d67e; the other two sites are inside one large function and are recorded as sites only

wrapper.note: three direct call sites, recorded as sites only; the wrapper is never tail-jumped to and never referenced through a function-pointer slot

object_layout.link: the qword at [outer+0x40]+0x30; the selector's object pointer is this value plus 0x40 (64-bit wrapping)
object_layout.outer_plus_0x40: outer+0x40, qword pointer to a struct whose +0x30 field holds the link value
object_layout.record_1: stack record built from the source: (source+0x20, source+0x28 - 8 wrapping)
object_layout.record_2: stack record built from the source: (source+0x40, source+0x48 - 8 wrapping)

return_value: 1 when the index is 0; otherwise the selector's result with its low bit flipped (xor $0x1), which for the selector's 0/1 contract is exactly NOT

semantics.nonzero_index_path: read outer+0x40, then the qword at that struct's +0x30; the selector object is that qword plus 0x40 (64-bit wrapping). Build record 1 as (source+0x20, source+0x28 - 8 wrapping) and record 2 as (source+0x40, source+0x48 - 8 wrapping) on the stack, call the selector 0x5f6c2a0 with (rdi = selector object, esi = index, rdx = record 1 pointer, rcx = record 2 pointer), and return the selector's result xor 1.
semantics.zero_index_path: the return register is preset to 1 and the index test (test edx,edx at 0x5ebd14d) jumps straight to the epilogue, so an index of 0 returns 1 without reading any object or source field and without calling the selector.

unknowns: The dispatch callee 0x5f6a820's semantics (what makes the selector return nonzero for an index) are not modelled here; the model treats selector results as oracle inputs.
Whether the selector or dispatch mutates the object is not pinned; the model treats all inputs as stable across one call.
The three wrapper call sites' caller functions are recorded as sites only; what each caller passes as the record source and index is not pinned by this item.

selector.identity: index selector: returns 0 when signed32(obj+0x14) <= index, otherwise picks the inline or heap slot and tail-jumps to dispatch 0x5f6a820

wrapper.identity: selector-inversion wrapper: zero-index fast path returning 1, otherwise one selector call whose result is inverted
